title: NVIDIA, Qualcomm join U.S., Indian VCs to help build India’s next deep tech startups
description: Qualcomm Ventures has joined six Indian venture firms, collectively adding more than $850 million to boost India’s deep-tech ecosystem.
author: Jagmeet Singh

title: Amazon sends legal threats to Perplexity over agentic browsing
description: Amazon won't allow agents on its site that don't identify themselves as such. Perplexity is not pleased.
author: Julie Bort, Rebecca Bellan

title: People Inc. forges AI licensing deal with Microsoft as Google traffic drops
description: People Inc. signs an AI licensing deal with Microsoft, which will use its media content in Copilot.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Rivian creates another spinoff company called Mind Robotics
description: It's the second time this year Rivian has spun out a new company, after it created micromobility startup Also in March.
author: Sean O'Kane

title: Google’s AI Mode gets new agentic capabilities to help book event tickets and beauty appointments
description: For example, you can ask "find me 2 cheap tickets for the Shaboozey concert coming up. prefer standing floor tickets." AI Mode will then search across multiple websites to find real-time ticket options that meet your specific requests.
author: Aisha Malik

title: Sora is now available on Android in the US, Canada, and other regions
description: The Sora app is now available for Android users in the US, Canada, and Japan, among other regions.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: Shopify says AI traffic is up 7x since January, AI-driven orders are up 11x
description: Shopify says AI-driven traffic to its online stores is up 7x since January, and orders from AI search are up 11x.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Anthropic projects $70B in revenue by 2028: Report
description: The Information reports that Anthropic expects to generate as much as $70 billion in revenue and $17 billion in cash flow in 2028. The growth projections are fueled by rapid adoption of Anthropic’s business products, a person with knowledge of the company’s financials said.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Nvidia, Deutsche Telekom strike €1B partnership for a data center in Munich
description: Nvidia has signed a €1 billion partnership with Deutsche Telekom to set up an "AI factory" in Munich that aims to boost Germany's AI computing power by 50%.
author: Ram Iyer

title: Alexa+ comes to the Amazon Music app
description: The feature is currently available across all Amazon Music subscription plans but is only available for users with Alexa+ Early Access.
author: Lauren Forristal

title: ClickUp adds new AI assistant to better compete with Slack and Notion
description: ClickUp has been trying to better compete with the likes of Notion, Slack, and Microsoft Teams by providing calendar, communication, documents, enterprise search, and task tracking under one product.
author: Ivan Mehta

title: Studio Ghibli and other Japanese publishers want OpenAI to stop training on their work
description: OpenAI's approach to working with copyrighted content is to ask forgiveness, not permission.
author: Amanda Silberling

title: Altman and Nadella need more power for AI, but they’re not sure how much
description: The CEOs of OpenAI and Microsoft are betting that AI will continue to consume more electricity, but they're not sure how much. That could leave some investors holding the bag.
author: Tim De Chant

title: Lambda inks multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure deal with Microsoft
description: This deal was announced just hours after Microsoft announced a $9.7 billion deal with Australian data center company IREN.
author: Rebecca Szkutak

title: Dia’s AI browser starts adding Arc’s ‘greatest hits’ to its feature set
description: Dia's AI browser has a head start on what works for consumers thanks to learnings from its browser experiment, Arc.
author: Sarah Perez

title: OpenAI and Amazon ink $38B cloud computing deal
description: OpenAI isn't done securing the AI infrastructure it needs to rapidly scale agentic workloads. The ChatGPT-maker on Monday said it has reached a deal with Amazon to buy $38 billion in cloud computing services over the next seven years.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Microsoft’s $15.2B UAE investment turns Gulf State into test case for US AI diplomacy
description: For the first time, the U.S. has granted Microsoft a license to export Nvidia chips to the UAE – a move that positions the country as both a proving ground for U.S. export-control diplomacy and a regional anchor of American AI influence.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Microsoft inks $9.7B deal with Australia’s IREN for AI cloud capacity
description: The deal will give Microsoft access to compute infrastructure built with Nvidia's GB300 GPUs, which will be deployed over phases through 2026.
author: Ram Iyer

title: LG founder’s grandson, production firm partner up to bring AI to filmmaking
description: Brian Koo’s Stock Farm Road and Utopai Studios have partnered up to form Utopai East, an AI-powered film production company.
author: Kate Park

title: Kevin Rose’s simple test for AI hardware — would you want to punch someone in the face who’s wearing it?
description: "As an investor, you kind of have to not only say, okay, cool tech, sure, but emotionally, how does it make me feel? And how does it make others feel around me?"
author: Connie Loizos

title: Google pulls Gemma from AI Studio after Senator Blackburn accuses model of defamation
description: Senator Martha Blackburn argued Gemma’s fabrications are “not a harmless ‘hallucination,’" but rather “an act of defamation produced and distributed by a Google-owned AI model.”
author: Anthony Ha

title: Sam Altman says ‘enough’ to questions about OpenAI’s revenue
description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman recently said that the company is doing “well more” than $13 billion in annual revenue — and he sounded a little testy when pressed on how it will pay for its massive spending commitments.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Meta has an AI product problem
description: Meta's AI spending is starting to make Wall Street nervous.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Rising energy prices put AI and data centers in the crosshairs
description: A majority of consumers say they’re worried about data centers driving up electricity costs. Is the industry prepared for a possible backlash?
author: Tim De Chant

title: AI researchers ’embodied’ an LLM into a robot – and it started channeling Robin Williams
description: AI researchers at Andon Labs embedded various LLMs in a vacuum robot to test how ready they were to be embodied. And hilarity ensued.
author: Julie Bort

title: AI mania tanks CoreWeave’s Core Scientific acquisition — it buys Python notebook Marimo
description: CoreWeave's failed buy of Core Scientific is another sign of an AI bubble. But it's still shopping.
author: Julie Bort

title: ChatGPT: Everything you need to know about the AI-powered chatbot
description: A timeline of ChatGPT product updates and releases, starting with the latest, which we’ve been updating throughout the year.
author: Kyle Wiggers, Cody Corrall, Alyssa Stringer, Kate Park

title: Equity Live: From $300M seed rounds to data center builds, AI is feeling bubbly
description: The Equity crew was live at TechCrunch Disrupt 2025! Hosts Kirsten Korosec, Max Zeff, and Anthony Ha took over the Builders Stage on Monday morning to kick off the event with the question everyone’s asking: are we in an AI bubble?  Between valuations that have tripled in months, $300M seed rounds, and $100B commitments flying […]
author: Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, Maxwell Zeff

title: AWS exceeds Wall Street’s expectations as demand for cloud infra remains high
description: AWS continues to see strong demand as companies gobble up its cloud infrastructure services in the age of AI.
author: Rebecca Szkutak

title: Perplexity strikes multi-year licensing deal with Getty Images
description: Perplexity’s agreement with Getty appears to legitimize some of the startup’s previous use of Getty’s stock photos. Perplexity came under fire last year for a series of plagiarism accusations from several news organizations.
author: Rebecca Bellan
